verification_rules: Все факты должны иметь источник с authority >= 'peer_reviewed' или 'primary_historical'
Температурные/числовые данные — только из peer-reviewed источников
Все URL проверены на доступность (архивные копии для старых источников)

sources.author: Cohen, A.J.
sources.title: The optical spectra of Fe³⁺ in amethyst quartz
claims: Fe³⁺ oxidation to Fe⁴⁺ by natural radiation creates color centers
Absorption bands at 357nm and 545nm produce purple color
Color centers are thermally unstable above 200°C

sources.author: Rossman, G.R.
sources.title: Colored varieties of the silica minerals
claims: Decolorization begins at ~200°C, accelerates at 300-400°C
Complete irreversible decolorization at 400-500°C
Reversible bleaching possible below 300°C with X-ray/gamma radiation

sources.author: Cheng, J. & Guo, J.
sources.title: Color variation and phase transition of natural amethyst by heat treatment
claims: At 380°C purple begins to fade, by 420°C nearly colorless
Phase transition α-quartz → β-quartz at 573°C destroys color centers irreversibly
At 560°C optimal 'Fancy Intense' citrine color achieved
At 580-600°C milky-opalescent appearance (destruction of S1-centers)

sources.author: Berthelot, M.
sources.title: Sur la decoloration de l'amethyste par la chaleur
sources.journal: Comptes Rendus de l'Académie des Sciences
claims: Amethyst decolorizes at 300°C with prolonged heating (~12 hours)
Color can be restored by X-ray irradiation after thermal bleaching

sources.author: Kunz, G.F.
sources.title: The Curious Lore of Precious Stones
claims: Amethyst was one of the five cardinal gems (ruby, sapphire, emerald, diamond, amethyst)
Price equaled half of sapphire before Brazilian discoveries
Brazilian deposits discovered in 1830s-1840s collapsed the market

sources.author: Pliny the Elder (Gaius Plinius Secundus)
sources.title: Naturalis Historia, Book XXXVII
claims: Amethyst sobriety belief called 'mendacia magorum' (falsehoods of the magicians)
No mention of Bacchus-Amethyst myth in original text
sources.original_latin: amethystos... a vino abstinere dicunt, quod est vanum

sources.author: Belleau, Rémi
sources.title: Les Amours et Nouveaux Eschanges des Pierres Precieuses
claims: Literary invention of the Bacchus and Amethyst myth
NOT an ancient Greek myth — created in French Renaissance poetry
sources.debunk_target: Popular misconception that Bacchus-Amethyst myth is ancient Greek

sources.author: Ellis, W.C.
sources.title: The Coloration and Decolorization of Amethyst
claims: Cites Berthelot's 300°C / 12-hour decolorization experiment
Confirms thermal reversibility below critical temperature

temperature_scale.note: All temperatures in Celsius. Sources: Cheng & Guo 2020, Rossman 1994, Berthelot 1900 (via Ellis 1933)

stages.effect: Color begins to fade, partially reversible on cooling
α-quartz → β-quartz phase transition, color centers permanently destroyed
